description: Me fascina pensar en las huellas que dejamos en el universo. En la Luna y Marte descansan máquinas que enviamos a descubrir lo desconocido; detrás de ellas hay sueños, preguntas y personas que se atrevieron a mirar más lejos. Con “Abandoned but not Forgotten” quiero rescatar esas historias. Hoy soy una manada de una sola persona y busco curiosos que aporten desde la ciencia, la narrativa, el arte o el desarrollo. No hace falta saberlo todo: basta con asombro y ganas de explorar juntos. 🌌🐾
summary: Still Out There is an interactive illustrated book about the machines humanity left on the Moon and Mars. Created for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, it transforms NASA mission records into stories about the people, engineering, and discoveries behind these distant explorers. Readers turn watercolor pages, navigate a constellation, and open mission cards with 3D models and links to NASA sources. Designed for students and curious readers, the project connects scientific information with the wonder of exploration: even when a machine falls silent, its story and what it taught us remain.
details:
Still Out There invites readers to open a digital storybook and travel from the Moon to Mars through the stories of real NASA missions. A constellation guides readers between chapters; turning pages reveals watercolor illustrations and narratives about why each machine was sent, what it did, and what it helped us learn.

Blue-star mission cards offer interactive 3D models, technical information, and links to NASA records. The experience works on desktop and mobile and offers English and Spanish. It is intended for students, educators, and anyone curious about space exploration.

We combined the warmth of a storybook with interactive web graphics to make space hardware feel less like a list of objects and more like a collection of human journeys. The narratives draw on NASA mission resources, including the National Space Science Data Coordinated Archive and NASA mission pages.

The project was built with TypeScript, Next.js, React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and GSAP. We used Blender and NASA 3D resources for models. AI tools assisted with research, writing and translation, coding and debugging, and creating watercolor artwork; the author directed and reviewed the work. AI-generated illustrations are marked with a visible “with IA” label. The demonstration video uses an instrumental soundtrack synthesized specifically for the presentation with code written with AI assistance.
